_slop_comment: ste-general does not run the allowlist, so it needs a denylist. The obvious
source is the standard's own non-approved list, but that list is the whole
non-approved vocabulary of English, not a slop list: it holds 'way', 'every',
'under', and 'load'. Using it whole gave 44 errors on a README that reads
fine, and a check nobody can act on is a check nobody reads.
So ste-general flags a word only when it is in slop_core below, or when the
build step's length test picks it out: at least slop_min_length characters
with a shorter approved replacement. That is the shape of the problem, a long
Latinate word standing in for a short plain one.
ste-strict is unaffected. It runs the full allowlist, where every word that is
not approved fails whatever its length.
